functions.name: uc_version
functions.signature: unsigned int uc_version(unsigned int *major, unsigned int *minor);
functions.description: Return the combined Unicorn API version as (major << 24 | minor << 16 | patch << 8 | extra). If major/minor pointers are non-NULL, they are filled with the API major/minor numbers. Intended to allow runtime version checks (compare with UC_MAKE_VERSION).
requirements: uc may be NULL (not used).
If major and/or minor are non-NULL, they must be valid writable pointers.

functions.name: uc_arch_supported
functions.signature: bool uc_arch_supported(uc_arch arch);
functions.description: Check whether the given architecture (UC_ARCH_*) is supported by the linked Unicorn library.
requirements: arch must be a valid uc_arch enum value.

functions.name: uc_open
functions.signature: uc_err uc_open(uc_arch arch, uc_mode mode, uc_engine **uc);
functions.description: Create a new Unicorn engine instance for a specific architecture and mode. On success, stores the handle in *uc.
requirements: arch must be a supported UC_ARCH_* value.
mode must be a valid combination for the selected architecture (see uc_mode).
uc must be a non-NULL writable pointer to receive the handle.

functions.name: uc_close
functions.signature: uc_err uc_close(uc_engine *uc);
functions.description: Close and free a Unicorn engine instance. After this call, the handle is invalid and must not be used.
requirements: uc must be a valid handle returned by uc_open.
Must only be called when no further Unicorn API calls will be made with uc (using uc after close may crash).

functions.name: uc_query
functions.signature: uc_err uc_query(uc_engine *uc, uc_query_type type, size_t *result);
functions.description: Query engine state such as current mode, page size, architecture, or whether emulation stopped due to timeout.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
type must be one of uc_query_type.
result must be a non-NULL writable pointer appropriate for the query (API uses size_t* to return).

functions.name: uc_ctl
functions.signature: uc_err uc_ctl(uc_engine *uc, uc_control_type control, ...);
functions.description: Generic control interface to get/set internal engine state (similar to ioctl). Variadic arguments depend on control (see uc_control_type and helper macros).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
control must be a valid uc_control_type constructed with UC_CTL_* macros indicating arg count and direction.
Caller must pass the exact number and types of arguments required by the specific control as documented; otherwise behavior is invalid.
Some controls have timing constraints, e.g., CPU model must be set before any Unicorn API is called except uc_open.

functions.name: uc_errno
functions.signature: uc_err uc_errno(uc_engine *uc);
functions.description: Return the last error code recorded for the engine (like errno). Value is not guaranteed to persist after being read.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.

functions.name: uc_strerror
functions.signature: const char *uc_strerror(uc_err code);
functions.description: Return a human-readable string describing a Unicorn error code.
requirements: code must be a uc_err value.

functions.name: uc_reg_write
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_write(uc_engine *uc, int regid, const void *value);
functions.description: Write a value to a CPU register.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regid must be a valid register ID for the current architecture/mode.
value must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of the correct size for the register.

functions.name: uc_reg_read
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_read(uc_engine *uc, int regid, void *value);
functions.description: Read a CPU register value into a caller-provided buffer.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regid must be a valid register ID for the current architecture/mode.
value must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer large enough to receive the register value.

functions.name: uc_reg_write2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_write2(uc_engine *uc, int regid, const void *value, size_t *size);
functions.description: Write a value to a CPU register with explicit size. On return, *size holds the number of bytes written.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regid must be a valid register ID for the current arch/mode.
value must point to at least *size bytes of data to write.
size must be a non-NULL pointer; on input contains available size, on output receives written size.

functions.name: uc_reg_read2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_read2(uc_engine *uc, int regid, void *value, size_t *size);
functions.description: Read a CPU register value with explicit buffer size. On return, *size holds the number of bytes read.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regid must be a valid register ID for the current arch/mode.
value must point to a buffer of at least *size bytes.
size must be a non-NULL pointer; on input contains buffer size, on output receives actual size read.

functions.name: uc_reg_write_batch
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_write_batch(uc_engine *uc, int const *regs, void *const *vals, int count);
functions.description: Write multiple register values in one call.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regs must point to an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must point to an array of count pointers to register-sized values.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_reg_read_batch
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_read_batch(uc_engine *uc, int const *regs, void **vals, int count);
functions.description: Read multiple register values in one call into provided buffers.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regs must point to an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must point to an array of count writable buffers of appropriate size for each register.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_reg_write_batch2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_write_batch2(uc_engine *uc, int const *regs, const void *const *vals, size_t *sizes, int count);
functions.description: Write multiple register values with explicit per-register sizes. On return, sizes[i] holds bytes written for each register.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regs must be an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must be an array of count pointers to data buffers.
sizes must be an array of count size_t values; on input contains available sizes, on output receives written sizes.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_reg_read_batch2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_reg_read_batch2(uc_engine *uc, int const *regs, void *const *vals, size_t *sizes, int count);
functions.description: Read multiple register values with explicit per-register buffer sizes. On return, sizes[i] holds bytes read for each register.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regs must be an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must be an array of count pointers to writable buffers of at least sizes[i] bytes.
sizes must be an array of count size_t values; on input contains buffer sizes, on output receives bytes read.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_mem_write
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_write(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, const void *bytes, uint64_t size);
functions.description: Write a range of bytes into emulated memory starting at address.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be mapped and writable; writes to unmapped/protected memory will fail/trigger errors.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be the number of bytes to write.

functions.name: uc_mem_read
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_read(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, void *bytes, uint64_t size);
functions.description: Read a range of bytes from emulated memory starting at address into the provided buffer.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be mapped and readable; reads from unmapped/protected memory will fail/trigger errors.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be the number of bytes to read.

functions.name: uc_vmem_read
functions.signature: uc_err uc_vmem_read(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uc_prot prot, void *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Read bytes from a virtual address after MMU translation using the specified access type (prot). Useful when a virtual-to-physical mapping is in effect.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
All pages involved must be memory-mapped with permissions allowing MMU translation for the specified prot; otherwise the MMU will not translate.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size is the number of bytes to read.
Note: prot denotes access type for TLB lookup and differs from underlying physical memory protections (see header note).

functions.name: uc_vmem_write
functions.signature: uc_err uc_vmem_write(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uc_prot prot, void *bytes, size_t size);
functions.description: Write bytes to a virtual address after MMU translation using the specified access type (prot).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
All pages must be memory-mapped with permissions allowing MMU translation for the specified prot; otherwise translation will not occur.
bytes must point to a buffer of at least size bytes containing data to write.
size is the number of bytes to write.
Note: When translation succeeds for the given prot, the write occurs regardless of the mapping’s physical protections (see header note).

functions.name: uc_vmem_translate
functions.signature: uc_err uc_vmem_translate(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uc_prot prot, uint64_t *paddress);
functions.description: Translate a virtual address to a physical address using the MMU with the specified access type (prot).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must refer to mapped pages whose permissions allow MMU translation for the specified prot.
paddress must be a non-NULL writable pointer to receive the physical address.

functions.name: uc_emu_start
functions.signature: uc_err uc_emu_start(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t begin, uint64_t until, uint64_t timeout, size_t count);
functions.description: Start emulating instructions from begin until one of the stopping conditions is met: reaching until, timing out (microseconds), executing count instructions, a hook requests stop, or an error/exception occurs. If exits mechanism is enabled via uc_ctl, until is ignored.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle with code and state properly initialized.
begin should be a valid executable address; code must be mapped with execute permission.
until is the stop address (inclusive) unless exits are enabled (then ignored).
timeout is in microseconds; 0 means no timeout.
count is the instruction limit; 0 means run until completion.
Internal state is guaranteed correct only if uc_emu_start returns without errors or errors were handled in callbacks.

functions.name: uc_emu_stop
functions.signature: uc_err uc_emu_stop(uc_engine *uc);
functions.description: Request to stop an ongoing emulation started by uc_emu_start. Typically called from hook callbacks.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.

functions.name: uc_hook_add
functions.signature: uc_err uc_hook_add(uc_engine *uc, uc_hook *hh, int type, void *callback, void *user_data, uint64_t begin, uint64_t end, ...);
functions.description: Register a callback for one or more hook events (code, memory, interrupts, invalid instructions, TCG opcode, TLB fill, etc.). Applies to addresses in [begin, end] inclusive; if begin > end, applies globally for that type. Extra varargs depend on hook type (e.g., instruction ID for UC_HOOK_INSN, opcode and flags for UC_HOOK_TCG_OPCODE).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
hh must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the hook handle.
type is a bitmask of uc_hook_type values appropriate for the callback being registered.

callback must have the signature appropriate to the hook type (e.g., uc_cb_hookcode_t for UC_HOOK_CODE, uc_cb_hookmem_t for UC_HOOK_MEM_READ/WRITE/FETCH, uc_cb_eventmem_t for UNMAPPED/PROT, uc_cb_hookintr_t for UC_HOOK_INTR, uc_cb_hookinsn_invalid_t for UC_HOOK_INSN_INVALID, uc_hook_edge_gen_t for UC_HOOK_EDGE_GENERATED, uc_hook_tcg_op_2/uc_hook_tcg_sub_t for UC_HOOK_TCG_OPCODE, uc_cb_tlbevent_t for UC_HOOK_TLB_FILL).
user_data is opaque and passed to the callback.
begin and end define the inclusive address range; if begin > end, the hook fires whenever that type is triggered.
If type == UC_HOOK_INSN, a valid instruction ID must be supplied as an extra argument (currently only certain x86 insns supported: in, out, syscall, sysenter, cpuid).
If type == UC_HOOK_TCG_OPCODE, extra arguments are (uc_tcg_op_code opcode, uc_tcg_op_flag flags).

functions.name: uc_hook_del
functions.signature: uc_err uc_hook_del(uc_engine *uc, uc_hook hh);
functions.description: Unregister a previously added hook. After this call the hook handle is invalid.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
hh must be a valid hook handle previously returned by uc_hook_add.

functions.name: uc_mem_map
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_map(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uint32_t perms);
functions.description: Map a new zero-initialized memory region in the emulator at the given address and size with specified permissions.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be 4KB-aligned, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
size must be a multiple of 4KB, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
perms must be a combination of UC_PROT_READ | UC_PROT_WRITE | UC_PROT_EXEC, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
Region must not overlap incompatible existing mappings.

functions.name: uc_mem_map_ptr
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_map_ptr(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uint32_t perms, void *ptr);
functions.description: Map an existing host memory buffer into the emulator at the given address/size with specified permissions.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be 4KB-aligned, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
size must be a multiple of 4KB, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
perms must be a combination of UC_PROT_READ | UC_PROT_WRITE | UC_PROT_EXEC, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
ptr must point to host memory of at least size bytes and be mapped with at least PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE; otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: uc_mmio_map
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mmio_map(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uc_cb_mmio_read_t read_cb, void *user_data_read, uc_cb_mmio_write_t write_cb, void *user_data_write);
functions.description: Map an MMIO region handled by user-provided read/write callbacks.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be 4KB-aligned, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
size must be a multiple of 4KB, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
read_cb and write_cb must be valid function pointers implementing the MMIO semantics expected by the emulated code; user_data_* are passed back to them.

functions.name: uc_mem_unmap
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_unmap(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uint64_t size);
functions.description: Unmap an existing emulation memory region.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be 4KB-aligned, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
size must be a multiple of 4KB, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
The specified range must correspond to previously mapped memory.

functions.name: uc_mem_protect
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_protect(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t address, uint64_t size, uint32_t perms);
functions.description: Change permissions on an existing mapped memory region.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
address must be 4KB-aligned, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
size must be a multiple of 4KB, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
perms must be a combination of UC_PROT_READ | UC_PROT_WRITE | UC_PROT_EXEC, otherwise UC_ERR_ARG.
The specified range must already be mapped.

functions.name: uc_mem_regions
functions.signature: uc_err uc_mem_regions(uc_engine *uc, uc_mem_region **regions, uint32_t *count);
functions.description: Retrieve a snapshot of all mapped memory regions. Allocates an array of uc_mem_region which must be freed by uc_free().
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
regions must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an allocated array; free with uc_free().
count must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of entries.

functions.name: uc_context_alloc
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_alloc(uc_engine *uc, uc_context **context);
functions.description: Allocate an opaque context object for saving/restoring CPU context for the given engine.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
context must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the allocated uc_context.
Contexts may not be shared across engine instances with differing architectures or modes.

functions.name: uc_free
functions.signature: uc_err uc_free(void *mem);
functions.description: Free memory allocated by uc_mem_regions. Note: uc_context_alloc-allocated contexts must be freed with uc_context_free (using uc_free on them is undefined).
requirements: mem must be a pointer previously returned via uc_mem_regions (i.e., the regions array).
Do not use to free uc_context objects (use uc_context_free).

functions.name: uc_context_save
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_save(uc_engine *uc, uc_context *context);
functions.description: Save the current CPU context of the engine into the provided context handle.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
context must be a valid uc_context allocated by uc_context_alloc for this engine.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_write
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_write(uc_context *ctx, int regid, const void *value);
functions.description: Write a register in a saved/restorable context object (not the live engine).
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context allocated by uc_context_alloc.
regid must be a valid register ID for the context’s arch/mode.
value must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of the correct register size.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_read
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_read(uc_context *ctx, int regid, void *value);
functions.description: Read a register value from a context object into caller-provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regid must be a valid register ID for the context’s arch/mode.
value must point to a buffer large enough for the register value.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_write2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_write2(uc_context *ctx, int regid, const void *value, size_t *size);
functions.description: Write a register value into a context with explicit size; on return *size holds bytes written.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regid must be valid for the context’s arch/mode.
value must point to at least *size bytes of data.
size must be non-NULL; on input provides available size, on output receives written size.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_read2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_read2(uc_context *ctx, int regid, void *value, size_t *size);
functions.description: Read a register value from a context with explicit buffer size; on return *size holds bytes read.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regid must be valid for the context’s arch/mode.
value must point to a buffer of at least *size bytes.
size must be non-NULL; on input provides buffer size, on output receives bytes read.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_write_batch
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_write_batch(uc_context *ctx, int const *regs, void *const *vals, int count);
functions.description: Write multiple registers into a context in one call.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regs must point to an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must point to an array of count pointers to register-sized values.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_read_batch
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_read_batch(uc_context *ctx, int const *regs, void **vals, int count);
functions.description: Read multiple registers from a context into provided buffers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regs must point to an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must point to an array of count writable buffers of appropriate sizes.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_write_batch2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_write_batch2(uc_context *ctx, int const *regs, const void *const *vals, size_t *sizes, int count);
functions.description: Write multiple registers into a context with per-register sizes; on return sizes[i] holds bytes written for each.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regs must be an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must be an array of count pointers to data.
sizes must be an array of count size_t values; on input provides available sizes, on output receives written sizes.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_context_reg_read_batch2
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_reg_read_batch2(uc_context *ctx, int const *regs, void *const *vals, size_t *sizes, int count);
functions.description: Read multiple registers from a context with per-register buffer sizes; on return sizes[i] holds bytes read for each.
requirements: ctx must be a valid uc_context.
regs must be an array of count valid register IDs.
vals must be an array of count pointers to writable buffers sized at least sizes[i].
sizes must be an array of count size_t values; on input provides buffer sizes, on output receives read sizes.
count must be non-negative; arrays must be at least count in length.

functions.name: uc_context_restore
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_restore(uc_engine *uc, uc_context *context);
functions.description: Restore the engine’s current CPU context from a previously saved context.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
context must be a valid uc_context previously used with uc_context_save and compatible with this engine instance.

functions.name: uc_context_size
functions.signature: size_t uc_context_size(uc_engine *uc);
functions.description: Return the size needed to store the CPU context. Can be used to allocate a raw buffer if saving directly (outside this header’s higher-level APIs).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.

functions.name: uc_context_free
functions.signature: uc_err uc_context_free(uc_context *context);
functions.description: Free a context allocated by uc_context_alloc.
requirements: context must be a uc_context previously returned by uc_context_alloc.
Do not pass memory allocated by uc_mem_regions here.

functions.name: uc_ctl_get_mode
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_get_mode(uc_engine *uc, int *mode) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_READ(UC_CTL_UC_MODE, 1), mode)
functions.description: Helper macro to read the current engine mode (UC_MODE_*) via uc_ctl.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
mode must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the mode.

functions.name: uc_ctl_get_page_size
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_get_page_size(uc_engine *uc, uint32_t *ptr) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_READ(UC_CTL_UC_PAGE_SIZE, 1), ptr)
functions.description: Helper macro to read the engine page size.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
ptr must be a non-NULL pointer to uint32_t.

functions.name: uc_ctl_set_page_size
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_set_page_size(uc_engine *uc, uint32_t page_size) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_WRITE(UC_CTL_UC_PAGE_SIZE, 1), page_size)
functions.description: Helper macro to set the engine page size. Unicorn may adjust this value.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.

functions.name: uc_ctl_get_arch
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_get_arch(uc_engine *uc, int *arch) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_READ(UC_CTL_UC_ARCH, 1), arch)
functions.description: Helper macro to read the current architecture (UC_ARCH_*).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
arch must be a non-NULL pointer to int.

functions.name: uc_ctl_get_timeout
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_get_timeout(uc_engine *uc, uint64_t *ptr) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_READ(UC_CTL_UC_TIMEOUT, 1), ptr)
functions.description: Helper macro to read whether emulation stopped due to a timeout (result as boolean in *ptr).
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.
ptr must be a non-NULL pointer to uint64_t.

functions.name: uc_ctl_exits_enable
functions.signature: macro: uc_ctl_exits_enable(uc_engine *uc) -> uc_ctl(uc, UC_CTL_WRITE(UC_CTL_UC_USE_EXITS, 1), 1)
functions.description: Enable the exits mechanism so that uc_emu_start uses configured exits instead of the until parameter.
requirements: uc must be a valid engine handle.

import os
import random
from typing import List

# Target data type: raw bytes used as memory content buffers for uc_mem_write/read fuzzers.
# The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as the source for bytes that will be written into
# an already-mapped 4KB page. They cap per-call write/read sizes to <=256 bytes and sometimes
# seed up to 32 bytes. Providing a buffer with rich byte diversity and variable lengths helps
# exercise different paths while remaining valid arbitrary bytes.

ASCII_SETS = [
    b"",  # allow empty base to trigger padding logic in stub
    b"\x00",  # NUL-heavy
    b"\xff",  # 0xFF heavy
    b"A" * 16,
    b"\x00\xff" * 64,  # alternating extremes
    b"0123456789ABCDEF" * 8,
    bytes(range(256)),  # full 0..255 ramp
]

# Common interesting lengths the stub might use: up to 256 and sometimes 32 bytes.
INTERESTING_LENS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256]


def _biased_length(rnd: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose lengths that align with fuzzer limits (<=256). Occasionally larger to provide
    # extra data if the harness resizes (it does for writes), but keep <= 512 overall.
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        return rnd.choice(INTERESTING_LENS)
    return rnd.randint(1, 512)


def _make_pattern(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose a buffer by concatenating selected patterns and random chunks to reach n bytes.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n

    # Sometimes start with a known pattern
    if rnd.random() < 0.8:
        base = rnd.choice(ASCII_SETS)
        if base:
            reps = max(1, min(remaining // max(1, len(base)), 4))
            parts.append((base * reps)[:remaining])
            remaining -= len(parts[-1])

    # Add structured subpatterns
    while remaining > 0:
        choice = rnd.random()
        chunk_len = min(remaining, max(1, int(rnd.expovariate(1/32))))
        if choice < 0.2:
            # increasing ramp
            start = rnd.randrange(256)
            chunk = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(chunk_len))
        elif choice < 0.4:
            # repeating byte
            b = rnd.randrange(256)
            chunk = bytes([b]) * chunk_len
        elif choice < 0.6:
            # alternating two bytes
            a = rnd.randrange(256)
            b = rnd.randrange(256)
            chunk = bytes([a, b]) * (chunk_len // 2) + (bytes([a]) if chunk_len % 2 else b"")
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # printable ASCII with occasional NULs
            pool = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789\n\r\t\x00"
            chunk = bytes(pool[rnd.randrange(len(pool))] for _ in range(chunk_len))
        else:
            # fully random
            chunk = rnd.randbytes(chunk_len) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(chunk_len))
        parts.append(chunk)
        remaining -= len(chunk)

    data = b"".join(parts)

    # Occasionally prefix or suffix with zeros to mimic common memory patterns
    if rnd.random() < 0.3 and len(data) > 0:
        pad = min(len(data) // 8 + 1, 16)
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            data = (b"\x00" * pad) + data[:-pad]
        else:
            data = data[pad:] + (b"\x00" * pad)

    return data[:n]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a target length focusing on <=256 to match stub caps, but allow some variance.
    length = _biased_length(rnd)

    # Build the payload with rich patterns to exercise read/write paths without invalidity.
    payload = _make_pattern(rnd, length)

    # Ensure size cap per requirements (<4096)
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]

    return payload
